## Claims
- [source-backed] For bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the lower-adjoined family \(G=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- [proved] Let \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\) and \(m=\binom{a+b}{a}\). Then \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^m\) if and only if \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}(Q\otimes\mathbb Q)=m\).
- [proved] Under the equivalent rational-full-rank hypothesis, the images of \(G\) form a homogeneous integral basis of \(Q\), and
  \[
  \operatorname{Hilb}_{Q}(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_{z}.
  \]
- [proved] Minimality alone does not imply rational full rank: for \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(J=(2x,x^2)\), the irredundant family \(\{2x,x^2\}\) has \(J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2\), of rational rank \(1<2\).
- [unsupported] A uniform proof that \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}(J_v/A_+J_v)\otimes\mathbb Q=\binom{a+b}{a}\) is not supplied here.

## Strategy
This establishes the requested theory-to-generalization target as a conditional reduction of the unresolved torsion-freeness roadblock; the unconditional stronger statement is not established.

Let \(F=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z e_\rho\), mapped onto \(Q\) by
\(e_\rho\mapsto[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]\). Generation gives a surjection \(F\twoheadrightarrow Q\), and \(\operatorname{rank}F=m\). If \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}Q_{\mathbb Q}=m\), then \(F_{\mathbb Q}\to Q_{\mathbb Q}\) is an isomorphism. Its kernel \(K\) therefore satisfies \(K_{\mathbb Q}=0\). Since \(K\subseteq F\) is torsion-free, \(K=0\). Thus \(F\cong Q\). Applying the accepted indecomposable-basis lemma gives the claimed integral homogeneous basis.

Finally, \(|(i^j,\rho)|=ij+|\rho|\), while partitions \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) have enumerator \(\binom{a+b}{a}_z\), yielding the Hilbert series.

## Gaps
The exact missing premise is rational full rank of \(Q\), not a separate integral-primitivity assertion: with the known \(m\)-element generating surjection, rational full rank already forces integral freeness.

No conclusion is made for the right-adjoined family. The supplied theorem proves the lower-adjoined family; its discussion of the transposed family only indicates a possible transposition of arguments. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 827-840]

## Next
For one fixed parameter tuple, the smallest discriminating computation is rational only: in degrees \(ij,\ldots,ij+ab\), compute
\[
\dim_{\mathbb Q}J_{v,d}/(A_+J_v)_d
\]
from the complete multiplication-relation lattice and compare it with
\([z^{d-ij}]\binom{a+b}{a}_z\). Equality in every such degree decides the rational-full-rank premise for that tuple, but cannot prove the all-parameter statement.
